what: One-time exception for Steinbach North (C-3): gravity sewer, piped water, 32-ft concrete street, swale drainage with no curb and gutter, through the development agreement
reasons_against: Not a variance but a change to city specifications; sets a precedent that open ditches are acceptable in commercial zones; equal treatment of developers. Mayor Goertzen absent (declared perceived conflict).
source: transcript (no 2016 minutes); Zwaagstra stated 'I'm not even voting in favor of the motion'

what: Motion to deny subdivision 4451/2016-7705 (lot-line change, 275 Third Street / 4 Fernwood Bay) over drainage and servicing
result: Tie, motion lost; file then tabled
for: Councillor Penner (mover; which Penner unclear); Fehr
reasons_against: A mandatory lot-grading plan would deal with drainage and give the area a drainage plan it lacks; uneven lot lines exist elsewhere. Siemens absent; the third vote on each side not recorded.

what: Variance excusing a Park Road West tool-rental business on a gravel road from paving required parking
reasons_against: Paving was a condition of the 2015 permit and lot-grading plan; an outstanding work order; ignorance of the rule is not an excuse.
source: transcript; Zwaagstra later said 'a majority of council approved' (2018-10-02 1:07:21)

what: Zoning By-law 2100 surfacing option 2: sites abutting an unpaved road need only an all-weather surface for parking
reasons_against: Keeps the city's high urban standard; roads in front are eventually paved. C. Penner's motion to keep hard surfacing had no seconder.

what: Variance V-2018-24, 266 Park Road West: four required parking stalls need not be hard surfaced
for: S. Penner; Zwaagstra; Funk; Siemens; Goertzen; Fehr
reasons_against: Paving was required and agreed to in the original development; the principle of honouring signed agreements.

what: Second reading of By-law 2102, closing part of the Harmony Lane public reserve so it can be reconfigured
for: Zwaagstra; C. Penner; S. Penner; Goertzen
reasons_against: Neighbours bought relying on city maps showing the green space; the public hearing should give weight to residents; a smaller change to one lot line could have worked.

what: Deny side-yard variance V-2019-19 at 28 Alexander Way (Lexington Village) over drainage-swale risk
for: Zwaagstra; D. Penner; S. Penner; B. Hiebert; Funk
reasons_against: Siemens thought a corner lot posed little drainage risk and moved a 2-foot compromise that found no seconder (J. Hiebert absent).

what: Amendment to cut the Clearspring Greens pathway to limestone with no lighting
against: D. Penner; Zwaagstra; S. Penner; B. Hiebert; Funk
reasons_against: Majority: residents wanted lighting for safety, staff recommended it, and asphalt suits wheeled users; the real dispute was who pays.

what: First and second reading of By-law 2132, Clearspring Greens pathway local improvement (residents pay about 80%)
for: D. Penner; Zwaagstra; S. Penner; B. Hiebert; Funk
reasons_against: Siemens: first time residents would pay most of a pathway connecting them to the community; cost too high. J. Hiebert: supported a cheaper version to get something built.

what: Move Clearspring pathway lighting cost to the city's capital development reserve
for: Zwaagstra; B. Hiebert; S. Penner; D. Penner; J. Hiebert; Funk

what: First reading of By-law 2161, Acres Drive construction and water main local improvement
for: Zwaagstra; S. Penner; B. Hiebert; Funk; J. Hiebert
reasons_against: Siemens: the road benefits the whole city and the city's development corporation, which recovers costs through lot sales; Envision is a charity that gets no direct benefit.

what: Refuse a 3-way stop at Wyndham Estate Drive and Ashford Lane by the new Hampton Village park and middle school; add a no-stopping zone instead
for: Jac Siemens; Jake Hiebert; Damian Penner; Michael Zwaagstra; Bill Hiebert; Earl Funk
reasons_against: Susan Penner wanted a safe crossing near the school and new park, where there is no sidewalk on the other side.

what: Close the unbuilt First Street public lane and keep it as a public drain (By-law 2232), a condition of an approved subdivision
for: Michael Zwaagstra; Susan Penner; Bill Hiebert; Damian Penner; Earl Funk
reasons_against: Siemens voted against on principle over the CBD zero-lot-line zoning of the related project; Jake Hiebert gave no reason.

what: Deny a 4-foot side-yard variance on an annexed 4-acre lot at 317 PTH 52 West over drainage concerns
for: Jake Hiebert; Jac Siemens; Earl Funk; Susan Penner; Michael Zwaagstra

what: Approve a front-yard variance (17 ft vs 25 ft) on a corner duplex lot in the new Sterling Crescent subdivision, against the city engineer's stormwater advice
for: Jac Siemens; Bill Hiebert; Damian Penner; Susan Penner
against: Earl Funk; Jake Hiebert; Michael Zwaagstra
reasons_against: Extra stormwater runoff beyond the subdivision's design and a precedent for more encroachments (Zwaagstra, Funk); the size and look of the encroachment (a councillor in a merged speaker cluster, likely Jake Hiebert).

what: Approve variances for an older house at 225 Kroeker Avenue, including a 2.4-foot side yard the engineering department opposed, relying on a lot grading plan
result: Carried 4-1 as recorded (Jac Siemens excused; the mayor is not listed in the recorded vote)
for: Michael Zwaagstra; Damian Penner; Susan Penner; Bill Hiebert
reasons_against: A 2-foot side yard is not adequate for drainage or emergency access, and engineering opposed it.
